title: Training and Education Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) FMOS, CG TECOM
raw_text:
1. MOS 8802, Training and Education Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) FMOS, CG
TECOM

    a. Summary. Training and Education Officers serve as Systems Approach
to Training (SAT)/Instructional Systems Development (ISD) Specialists in
billets concerned with various training and education programs. These
assignments require a knowledge and understanding of educational leadership,
educational research and methodologies, education and training
administration, educational/training instructional technology, curriculum
development and evaluation, and management of instruction. This will be
assigned a FMOS only by the CMC (MM) to officers who have completed the
prescribed course of instruction under the provisions of the Advanced Degree
Program (ADP).

    b. Prerequisites. This MOS requires a graduate level degree in
Education. The proposed curriculum must include coursework in Adult Learning
Theory, Curriculum Development, Instructional Development/Design, Assessment
and Instructional Technology. These courses are the minimum requirement.
Additional courses may be identified, based on billet need, by the OccFld
manager.

    c. Requirements. Upon request and approval, this MOS may also be
assigned to officers possessing an advanced degree acquired prior to entry
into the service or through off-duty educational efforts.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Serves as the service-level representative to the operating
forces and supporting establishment on all issues relating to training
standards, training program development, unit training management/evaluation,
and unit training readiness.

        (2) Implements, evaluates and manages the procedures and policies of
Instructional Systems Design, and delivery and validation of instruction.

        (3) Reviews, investigates, introduces, and evaluates emerging
instructional strategies, methodologies, technologies, and techniques.

        (4) Coordinate and facilitate professional development opportunities
and training for instructors, faculty advisors, trainers, and those that
manage Marine Corps Formal Schools.

            (5) Reviews and evaluates programmed instructional materials.

        (6) Serves as an advisor on military and civilian related education
and training programs.

        (7) Conducts research in support of training and education plans and
programs.

        (8) Supervises the training and education testing policy and
promulgates pertinent orders.

        (9) Serves as a course(s) or school administrator manages and plans
short/long range budget, T/O and T/E, facilities, and Training Input Plan
(TIP), for a school.


                                         1-342                       Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Training and Development Managers 11-3042.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

matches: Oversee training programs.
Training and Education Officers serve as Systems Approach to Training (SAT)/Instructional Systems Development (ISD) Specialists in billets concerned with various training and education programs.
Discuss assigned duties with classroom teachers to coordinate instructional efforts.

These assignments require a knowledge and understanding of educational leadership, educational research and methodologies, education and training administration, educational/training instructional technology, curriculum development and evaluation, and management of instruction.
Participate in staffing decisions and direct training of subordinates.

d. Duties (1) Serves as the service-level representative to the operating forces and supporting establishment on all issues relating to training standards, training program development, unit training management/evaluation, and unit training readiness.
Research, evaluate, and prepare recommendations on curricula, instructional methods, and materials for school systems.
(2) Implements, evaluates and manages the procedures and policies of Instructional Systems Design, and delivery and validation of instruction.
Research and evaluate emerging instructional technologies or methods.
(3) Reviews, investigates, introduces, and evaluates emerging instructional strategies, methodologies, technologies, and techniques.
Plan and lead professional development activities for teachers, administrators, and support staff.
(4) Coordinate and facilitate professional development opportunities and training for instructors, faculty advisors, trainers, and those that manage Marine Corps Formal Schools.
Develop instructional materials, such as lesson plans, handouts, or examinations.
(5) Reviews and evaluates programmed instructional materials.
Oversee training programs.
(6) Serves as an advisor on military and civilian related education and training programs.
Provide analytical support for the design and development of training curricula, learning strategies, educational policies, or courseware standards.
(7) Conducts research in support of training and education plans and programs.
Train staff in regulatory policies or procedures.
(8) Supervises the training and education testing policy and promulgates pertinent orders.
Perform administrative or managerial functions, such as taking responsibility for a unit's staff, budget, planning, or long-range goals.
(9) Serves as a course(s) or school administrator manages and plans short/long range budget, T/O and T/E, facilities, and Training Input Plan (TIP), for a school.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
